key_insight: Explainable deep reinforcement learning can lower building electricity costs by learning transparent battery-control policies from real-time PV, demand, price, and forecast signals.
engineering_relevance: This work is relevant for smart building energy management because it combines optimization performance with post-hoc explanations that can improve trust and deployment of DRL controllers.
method: Trained on-policy and off-policy DRL agents for residential energy scheduling
Used an expanded state space with PV, battery, demand, tariff, weather, calendar, and forecast inputs
Applied post-hoc interpretation to explain learned control decisions
evidence_signal: The authors evaluated the framework on both synthetic data and real-world Living Lab Energy Campus data, finding A2C and PPO more stable and higher-reward than off-policy methods.
watch_item: Performance depends on forecast quality and operational data fidelity, so real-world deployment may be sensitive to noisy measurements and changing tariff or weather conditions.
paper_title: Explainable Data-driven Deep Reinforcement Learning Methods for Optimal Energy Management in Buildings
